section: Charter Acts of 1793, 1813, 1833 and 1853 - provisions and significance
subsections: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust
Trade monopoly - Act ending it in India, Act ending tea and China trade
Charter Act 1813 - education grant, missionaries' entry, significance statements
Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a major change introduced by the Charter Act of 1853 in the recruitment to the civil services?
o: Civil-service appointments were transferred to the provincial governments.
All civil-service appointments were made by the Board of Control without examination.
Appointments were reserved exclusively for university graduates nominated by the Directors.
The Directors' patronage was abolished and open competitive examination was introduced.
accepted.x: The Act abolished the patronage of the Court of Directors and introduced open competition for civil-service recruitment.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority whose patronage was removed and the method that replaced it.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The introduction of open competitive examination for the Indian Civil Service was supported by:
o: William Bentinck and T. B. Macaulay
accepted.x: Charles Trevelyan and Robert Lowe supported the introduction of open competitive examination for the civil services.
accepted.tq: Match the reform with the persons associated with it, avoiding a swap with missionary or legislative reformers.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Macaulay Committee on the Indian Civil Service:
1. It was constituted in 1854.
2. It favoured the replacement of nomination by competitive examinations.
3. It gave preference to university graduates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Macaulay Committee was constituted in 1854, recommended competitive examinations in place of nomination, and favoured university graduates.
accepted.tq: Check each recruitment reform separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Charter Act of 1853 separated the following functions of the Governor-General's Council:
accepted.x: The Act separated the legislative functions from the executive functions of the Governor-General's Council.
accepted.tq: Test the exact pair of functions instead of confusing it with the later separation of commercial functions.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the separate legislative arrangement created by the Charter Act of 1853, consider the following statements:
1. Six new legislative members were added.
2. The arrangement was described as a separate Central Legislative Council.
3. Four of the six members were appointed by the provincial governments of Madras, Bombay, Bengal and Agra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Act added six legislative members, creating a separate Central Legislative Council; four were appointed by the governments of Madras, Bombay, Bengal and Agra.
accepted.tq: Use composition statements to distinguish the new legislative body from the executive council.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The remaining two of the six new legislative members under the Charter Act of 1853 were:
o: The Secretary to the Board of Control and the Law Member
The Chief Justice and one judge of the Calcutta Supreme Court
The Governor of Bombay and the Governor of Madras
The Commander-in-Chief and the Finance Member
accepted.x: The Chief Justice and one judge of the Calcutta Supreme Court constituted the remaining two of the six new legislative members.
accepted.tq: Complete the numerical composition from the two judicial members rather than the provincial nominees.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The representation of the provincial governments of Madras, Bombay, Bengal and Agra in the legislative arrangement of 1853 is significant because it marked:
o: The first separation of the judiciary from the executive
The first direct election in India
accepted.x: The appointment of members by these provincial governments was regarded as the first local representation in the central legislative arrangement.
accepted.tq: Link the institutional composition with its stated constitutional significance.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The expression that the Indian territories of the East India Company were held “in trust” is associated with the:
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1853 continued the Company's authority over its Indian territories in trust for the British Crown, its heirs and successors.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Charter Acts by attaching the exact phrase to the correct year.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the tenure provision under the Charter Act of 1853?
o: The Company's authority was renewed without a fixed 20-year term, pending further provision by Parliament.
The Company was immediately deprived of all authority over Indian territories.
The Company's authority was renewed for a fixed period of 10 years.
The Company's authority was renewed for a fixed period of 20 years.
accepted.x: Unlike the earlier Charter Acts, the 1853 Act fixed no 20-year term; the territories were held in trust until Parliament provided otherwise.
accepted.tq: Compare the presence or absence of a fixed renewal period across the Charter Acts.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1853 - open competition, separate legislative functions, territories held in trust  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Act — Governor-General at the time
accepted.x: Lord Hastings was the Governor-General at the time of the Charter Act of 1813. Sir John Shore, William Bentinck and Dalhousie were associated with 1793, 1833 and 1853 respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Governor-General–Act pair and eliminate swapped names.
accepted.sec: Charter Act → key provision (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Charter Acts in chronological order:
A. Charter Act of 1833
B. Charter Act of 1793
C. Charter Act of 1853
D. Charter Act of 1813
accepted.x: The Charter Acts were passed in 1793, 1813, 1833 and 1853, giving the sequence B, D, A, C.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest Acts first, then place the two middle dates.
accepted.sec: Charter Act → key provision (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a provision of the Charter Act of 1793?
o: Open competitive examination was introduced for the civil services.
The Company's trade monopoly was ended in India except for tea and China trade.
The monopoly of trade was extended for 20 years.
The Company became a purely administrative body.
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the Company's monopoly of trade for 20 years.
accepted.tq: Match the earliest Charter Act with its distinctive renewal provision.
accepted.sec: Charter Act → key provision (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Charter Act of 1793 strengthened the control of the Governor-General over which presidencies?
accepted.x: The Act gave the Governor-General greater control over the presidencies of Bombay and Madras.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specific presidencies named in the provision from other administrative units.
accepted.sec: Charter Act → key provision (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Charter Act of 1793, the salaries of the Board of Control were paid from the:
accepted.x: The salaries of the Board of Control were charged to the Indian exchequer under the Charter Act of 1793.
accepted.tq: Identify the source of payment rather than confusing it with the body receiving the payment.
accepted.sec: Charter Act → key provision (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Commander-in-Chief under the Charter Act of 1793 is correct?
o: He was ordinarily excluded from the Governor-General's Council.
He replaced the Governor-General as head of the Council.
He was given the exclusive power to appoint council members.
He was compulsorily made a member of the Governor-General's Council.
accepted.x: The Commander-in-Chief was not ordinarily a member of the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1793.
accepted.tq: Look for the qualifying word “ordinarily” instead of converting a limited rule into an absolute one.
accepted.sec: Charter Act → key provision (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Charter Act of 1833 — Company retained all commercial functions
Charter Act of 1793 — Monopoly extended for 20 years
Charter Act of 1813 — Education grant of one lakh rupees annually
Charter Act of 1853 — Territories held in trust
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company's commercial functions and made it a purely administrative body.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed or negated provision in an otherwise familiar Act–feature list.
accepted.sec: Charter Act → key provision (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly in India but retained its exclusive right to trade in:
accepted.x: The Act ended the general trade monopoly in India but retained the Company's exclusive trade in tea and with China.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to a broad statement instead of accepting that the entire monopoly ended.
accepted.sec: Trade monopoly - Act ending it in India, Act ending tea and China trade  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Company's exclusive right to trade in tea and with China was abolished by the:
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1833 removed the Company's remaining monopoly over tea trade and trade with China.
accepted.tq: Separate the general Indian trade monopoly from the later tea-and-China exception.
accepted.sec: Trade monopoly - Act ending it in India, Act ending tea and China trade  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Trade monopoly — Act ending it
o: General trade with India — Charter Act of 1813
General trade with India — Charter Act of 1833
Tea trade and trade with China — Charter Act of 1813
Tea trade and trade with China — Charter Act of 1793
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's general trade monopoly with India, while the 1833 Act ended its tea and China trade monopoly.
accepted.tq: Start from the general-trade pair and distinguish it from the retained exception.
accepted.sec: Trade monopoly - Act ending it in India, Act ending tea and China trade  [other exams]

accepted.s: The annual sum provided by the Charter Act of 1813 for education was:
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1813 provided one lakh rupees, or Rs 1,00,000, annually for education-related purposes.
accepted.tq: Read the place value carefully and reject the ten-lakh distractor.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1813 - education grant, missionaries' entry, significance statements  [other exams]

accepted.s:
The education grant under the Charter Act of 1813 was intended for which of the following purposes?
1. Revival of literature
2. Encouragement of learned natives
3. Promotion of science

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The annual grant was intended for the revival of literature, encouragement of learned natives and promotion of science.
accepted.tq: Treat the listed purposes as separate components of one grant before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1813 - education grant, missionaries' entry, significance statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Charter Act of 1813 is regarded as the first step towards the principle of:
o: Complete separation of education from government
accepted.x: The education grant under the Act marked the first step towards recognising State responsibility for education.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional significance of the grant rather than merely its amount.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1813 - education grant, missionaries' entry, significance statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the significance of the Charter Act of 1813 in relation to Christian missionaries?
o: It officially sanctioned the entry of missionaries and propagation of Christianity in India.
It prohibited missionaries from entering India.
It transferred missionary activities exclusively to provincial governments.
It permitted only commercial agents to enter India.
accepted.x: Under Evangelical pressure and the influence of figures such as William Wilberforce and Charles Grant, the Act allowed missionaries to enter India and propagate Christianity.
accepted.tq: Distinguish official permission for missionary activity from commercial or administrative provisions.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1813 - education grant, missionaries' entry, significance statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: The missionary provision in the Charter Act of 1813 was associated with pressure from:
o: Judges of the Calcutta Supreme Court alone
accepted.x: The missionary provision reflected Evangelical pressure, including that of William Wilberforce and Charles Grant, as well as Utilitarian influence.
accepted.tq: Match the policy pressure with the ideological groups named in the provision.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1813 - education grant, missionaries' entry, significance statements  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813 are correct?
1. It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company's Indian possessions.
2. It made civil-servant training compulsory.
3. It extended the Charter for 20 years.
4. It mandated public education as part of Company governance in Andhra.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements describe provisions or significance associated with the Charter Act of 1813, including its application to public education as part of Company governance in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Check the general constitutional, administrative and regional implications together rather than isolating the education grant.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1813 - education grant, missionaries' entry, significance statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Charter Act of 1833 conferred exclusive legislative power for all British India on the:
o: Board of Control without the Governor-General
Provincial governments of Bombay and Madras
accepted.x: The Governor-General-in-Council received exclusive legislative power for all British India, and the presidencies lost their law-making powers.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority received the power, using the wrong-body trap for the distractors.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]

accepted.s: After the Charter Act of 1833, laws made by the central authority were called:
accepted.x: The legislation enacted by the central authority came to be called Acts; earlier laws had been known as Regulations.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the earlier and later official legislative terms.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Law Member added to the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833 was the:
o: Third member, and the first was Lord Hastings
Fourth member, and the first was T. B. Macaulay
Sixth member, and the first was Robert Lowe
Fifth member, and the first was Charles Trevelyan
accepted.x: The Law Member was the fourth member of the Governor-General's Council, and T. B. Macaulay was the first to hold the position.
accepted.tq: Combine the numerical position with the first office-holder to avoid a swapped-person option.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the first Law Commission in India:
1. It was established in 1834.
2. It was under the chairmanship of T. B. Macaulay.
3. It drafted the Indian Penal Code.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The first Law Commission was established in 1834 under Macaulay and drafted the Indian Penal Code.
accepted.tq: Verify the year, chairmanship and principal legal work as three linked facts.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]

accepted.s: Section 87 of the Charter Act of 1833 provided that no Indian should be barred from office on the grounds of:
o: Province, gender, tribe or political opinion
Religion, place of birth, descent or colour
accepted.x: Section 87 declared that religion, place of birth, descent or colour should not bar an Indian from holding office.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact four grounds instead of substituting broader modern equality categories.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]

accepted.s: The part of the Bengal Presidency separated and placed under the Agra Presidency by the Charter Act of 1833 was later renamed the:
accepted.x: The separated territory was placed under the Agra Presidency in 1834 and was renamed the North-Western Provinces in 1836.
accepted.tq: Link the administrative reorganisation with its later official name, not with a neighbouring province.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Charter Act of 1833?
o: It represented the final step towards centralisation and made the Company purely administrative.
It abolished the office of the Governor-General of Bengal without creating a successor.
It was the first Charter Act to renew the Company's authority for a fixed 20-year term.
It restored the law-making powers of the presidencies.
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1833 is regarded as the final step towards centralisation and converted the Company into a purely administrative body.
accepted.tq: Combine the distinctive significance and institutional consequence of the Act.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the Act from which the Ministry of Law and Justice, described as the oldest organ of the Government of India, traces its origin?
accepted.x: The Ministry of Law and Justice traces its origin to the Charter Act of 1833, which introduced the Law Member and the first Law Commission.
accepted.tq: Connect the modern institutional legacy with the historical Act that created its legal foundation.
accepted.sec: Charter Act 1833 - title changes, end of commercial functions, Law Member, Law Commission, Agra Presidency  [other exams]
